conversations.answer: To run unit tests, you can use a testing library like Jest, a JavaScript Testing Framework. It allows you to create, run and structure tests.Here are the steps to set up Jest:Firstly, initialize a Node.js project by creating a package.json. You can do this by running the command npm init -y in your project root directory. This will automatically create a package.json file with default values.Then, you need to install Jest. You can install it using the npm package manager with the following command: npm install --save-dev jest.Your package.json should then look like this:[CODE_BLOCK_0]Next, update your game.js file to make it module-friendly (so that it can be imported in other js files). You can do this by modifying it as shown below:[CODE_BLOCK_1]Your game.test.js file seems fine, it will import the startPlaying function and checks if it's defined.Finally, run the test by using the following command: npm run test.However, since you're using jQuery in the code, you might face issues with the Jest environment because it doesn't have access to the DOM. In that case, you would need to use something like jsdom (a JavaScript based headless browser that can create a realistic testing environment) and mock the jQuery syntax.Here is a simple example of how you could test your startPlaying function:[CODE_BLOCK_2]This code creates a mock for jQuery and then calls startPlaying. It then checks if the function is working as expected and returns the correct result.Remember to install jest and jsdom in your project using npm:[CODE_BLOCK_3]Please note that running a front-end unit test without a browser context can be tricky, and the given mock example is a simplification of the reality. In a more complex scenario, you would probably use tools such as Jest with additional libraries (like Enzyme or Testing Library) that help handle React components, virtual DOM and many other things to provide a more complete testing environment.

conversations.answer: The error "ReferenceError: alert is not defined" happens because the alert function is part of the window object in a browser environment. When running Jest, it uses a Node.js environment, which does not have a window object or any of its methods (like alert).In a test environment, it's best to avoid using these kinds of functions that rely on the browser. But if you absolutely need to use something like alert, you can mock it out for testing. However, a better approach might be to refactor your code to not rely on such methods.Let's refactor your code to return the string message instead of alerting it, which will allow us to test the result.Here's your updated game.js:[CODE_BLOCK_0]And the test file game.test.js would look like this:[CODE_BLOCK_1]Now when you run npm run test, Jest will call the function startPlaying and compare the return value with the expected string "You selected: 1".Please note that such kind of changes where we change our original code to accommodate testing are not always the best solution. In real projects, you would want to structure your code in a way that makes it easy to test and avoid functions that are difficult to test like alert.
